result:
The three roaming chains now read exactly as B0147 writes them, each as one five-node line. One required integration test fails, but it fails the same way at HEAD `4372448` without my change.

- **Chain 1:** `Low activation -> Proposition + journey -> Pass redesign + digital activation -> Attach rate / activation -> Revenue uplift`
- **Chain 2:** `High complaints -> Journey + service assurance -> Proactive comms + QoS monitoring -> Complaint rate -> CX + care cost`
- **Chain 3:** `Partner cost pressure -> Partner model + analytics -> Partner optimization -> Cost/MB, margin -> Margin improvement`

**What changed** (uncommitted, as asked):
- **KPIs and benefits:** the three chain KPIs are renamed and the three chain benefits retitled to B0147's own words. Every business-case text that used the old names is updated. No number changed and all values stay synthetic.
- **Chain links:** each chain's contribution now points straight at its KPI, so the line goes initiative → KPI with no extra outcome step. The seed also stops with an error if a KPI or benefit name ever drifts from B0147.
- **New test:** `apps/api/test/integration/environment/demo-traceability-chains.test.ts` seeds the demo database, starts the real API, and calls `getTraceability`, the same operation the web traceability screen uses. It checks all three literal lines, plus two refusals: a user without read access and an anonymous request. With the old chain link (outcome KPI unset) its three chain cases fail, so the test does detect the old six-node chains.
- **Existing demo tests:** updated to the new names. In `demo-roaming.test.ts` I only changed my own `REQ-PB-090` block.

There is no migration, no new endpoint, no contract or schema change and no new dependency. I routed no operations, so the pending list is unchanged.

**Checks**

| Check | Exit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `validate.mjs --historical --stage DG4` (start and end) | 0 | PASS |
| `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm openapi:lint` | 0 | all pass |
| Prettier check | 0 | first two attempts flagged my own files; fixed with `prettier --write`, then passed |
| `packages/db` unit tests, locale unset and `C.UTF-8` | 0 | 72/72 each time |
| Required integration set | **1** | 250 of 251 passed |
| New test plus `demo-roaming.test.ts` on their own | 0 | 74/74 |

`pnpm lint` ran before the formatting fix, so I re-ran eslint on the three reformatted files (exit 0). The repository-wide `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:integration` and the full e2e suite were not run, per D-164.

**The one failure:** in `a02-a21-complete-lifecycle`, the new-transformation intake procedure gets `draft_charter (TL): 404 not_found`. That path has nothing to do with chain names. My first attempt to check it without my change was refused by the sandbox (the git index is read-only), so that run actually included my change; its log is named for what it really is. I then put the HEAD versions of my six files back by hand, re-ran `a02`, got the same failure, and restored my files byte-for-byte. It needs an owner — probably the T-DG5-BE-T5B line, but please confirm.

**For the orchestrator:**
- **`roaming.ts`** (not in my files): each chain's outcome statement is still the KPI text, so in the whole graph an outcome and its KPI share a label, and a comment there is now inaccurate. Neither is on the line, so the acceptance is met; the handback suggests a one-line fix for that file's owner.
- **D-168** is not in `docs/delivery/decisions.md`; it is only cited in the W22 assignments.
- **Untracked files:** the top-level dotfiles (`.bashrc`, `.mcp.json`, …) and `CLAUDE.local.md` are sandbox artifacts, not mine; don't integrate them.

The handback is at `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG5/T-DG5-BE-T6-backend-workflow-engineer.md`, and all logs are in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG5/T-DG5-BE-T6-evidence/`.
